correctness.rationale: The readout is first entry into a periodic orbit, not time of last excitation. Within each shore, the initial color classes remain internally synchronized. For any subset of classes the test ‘sum of sizes ≥2’ is unchanged by capping each size at 2. This preserves each active class's entire itinerary: with class membership fixed, equality of class-state tuples is equivalent to equality of full labelled states. I wrote and ran a separate bitset simulator on all 676 admissible signatures; it reproduced the full (preperiod, least period) table and verified the thin–fat predicate on every signature, with 24 signatures of preperiod 5 and all 24 eventually fixed. Direct labelled simulations included K_(3,4), where 144 of 2187 states have preperiod 5 and no periodic orbit is nonconstant. In one orientation the fat part contributes P_a ways and the thin part contributes 2Q_b; the reverse case is disjoint since thin parts have fewer than two excited vertices. The two forbidden excited-count ranges used for the closed form of P_n are disjoint for n≥3, and P_n/3^n→1. Fat needs at least four vertices and thin at least three, yielding the exact size boundary, including smaller positive shores.
residual_risks: The labelled tests on individual bicliques are illustrative. All sizes are covered by the proof of the quotient and complete 676-signature check together.

evidence: Restrict the displayed exponential sum to (t,p)=(5,1): its table factors in each orientation into the sum of the six fat weights and the two thin weights. Their exponential coefficients are P_n and 2Q_n, respectively; the thin weight is 2z(exp(z)−1−z).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Regrouping these terms gives 2(P_aQ_b+Q_aP_b), including 144 for (3,4); the balanced equivalent follows from the binomial tail. A five-step bound and recurrent counts alone would not imply these facts; the explicitly tabulated complete census does.
